items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: especially where Lincoln had made his famous speech about the freedom of mankind.

ctx.x: It was embarrassing to us and I think that the chauffeur of the bus should have told us because he must have known about the situation as we certainly could not have been the first Negroes to pass through Gettysburg on a Greyhound bus. The girl that had given us the seat must have been new in the restaurant and she was probably also embarrassed.

I had eaten in white restaurants in Michigan and New York and I just could not believe that something like that could have happened in Gettysburg which is in a Northern State and especially where Lincoln had made his famous speech about the freedom of mankind.
Of course the situation did not upset us and after we had eaten in the Greek restaurant, we came back to the bus to continue the journey as if nothing had happened.
